transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what brings you in to see me?

Um, yeah—thanks. I guess what made me come in is work stuff, mostly. I keep starting things I know are important, like the sanitation steps or batch logs or the end-of-line paperwork, and I’ll get most of it done, but then somehow I miss the last part or don’t finish it all the way.

I know that sounds kind of careless, and I really don’t mean it to be. I do know my job depends on doing it correctly, so it’s been worrying me. I just thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
When you leave that last step unfinished, is it usually because your attention drifted to something else, or because you deliberately stopped or avoided finishing it for some reason?

I don’t think I’m doing it on purpose, no. I’m not trying to avoid it or anything. It’s more like… I start the shift really meaning to stay focused and do everything right, and then after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels kind of all run together.

Sometimes I’ll realize I’ve been looking at the same tray or the same log sheet, but I’m not really taking in what I’m supposed to do next. And then that’s when the last step can get missed. I know that probably sounds bad, but it doesn’t feel deliberate.
Has this kind of trouble staying focused on tasks been something you've noticed since you were younger, or is this a new change for you, say in the last few months?

I don’t think it’s brand new, no. I mean, it feels more noticeable now because work is stricter, but my mom actually still has some of my elementary school report cards—around fourth grade, I think—that said I was bright, but needed a lot of reminders to finish classwork and turn in homework.

I remember understanding what we were learning, so it wasn’t like I couldn’t do it. But if the teacher gave instructions and then moved on, I’d miss pieces unless they were kind of nearby or checking in. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it has been there for a long time, I guess.
Outside of work, do you notice similar trouble finishing things or staying focused—like at home, when managing bills or paperwork, or reading something for a while?

Yeah… I mean, I notice it most at work, honestly. That’s where it matters the most, so maybe I’m more aware of it there.

Even when I start a shift really trying to stay locked in, after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels all kind of blur together. I’ll realize I’ve been staring at the same tray or the log sheet, but I’m not really taking in what I’m supposed to do next. I don’t know if that answers what you’re asking, but that’s the main way I notice it.

Can you give me a specific recent example of losing track partway through a task at home—like paying a bill, doing laundry, or reading something—rather than just noticing you feel more focused at work?

Um… I’m trying to think of a good home example. I know you asked about bills or laundry, and I don’t want to dodge the question, but the clearest one that comes to mind is still kind of the same pattern I notice at work.

Like I’ll start out really trying to stay locked in and do the steps properly, but after a while the cutting, weighing, and checking labels just sort of blur together. Then I’ll catch myself staring at the same tray or the log sheet, and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

At home it’s less obvious to me because there isn’t someone checking each step, if that makes sense. Sorry, I know that may not be exactly the example you asked for.

Think about something unrelated to work, like reading a book, watching a movie, or having a conversation with a friend—do you ever notice your mind drifting or losing track partway through in those situations too?

Yeah, I think so… I’m sorry, I know you asked about books or movies, and I’m not trying to avoid it. The clearest way I can explain it is still like what happens at work.

I’ll start out really trying to pay attention and do everything in order, but after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels kind of run together. Then I realize I’ve been looking at the same tray or the log sheet and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

So… yes, my mind does drift, I guess. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of example you mean.

Can you tell me about one specific time in the last week or two—like while watching a show, texting a friend, or filling out something at home—when you noticed your mind wander before you finished it?

I’m sorry, I’m kind of blanking on a clean home example, and I don’t want to make one up just to answer better.

The specific one I can actually picture was during a shift last week. I started out really trying to stay focused and keep the steps straight, but after a while the cutting, weighing, and checking labels all just sort of blended together. Then I realized I was just staring at the same tray and the log sheet, but I wasn’t really processing what I was supposed to do next.

I know that’s work again, not a show or texting, but that’s the clearest recent example I can honestly give.
Outside of work, do you often lose track of personal items like your keys or phone, or forget appointments and things you were supposed to do?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if it’s “often” in the way you mean, but I do lose stuff I need, especially on the floor at work.

Like my cut glove, or marker, or badge, or safety glasses—I’ll be sure I literally just had it in my hand, and then it’s gone. Then I end up retracing where I walked or checking the same spots for like ten minutes. It feels kind of embarrassing because it’s not like it went far, I just somehow lose track of it.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still, or find yourself interrupting others or acting on impulse without thinking it through?

Um… not really, I don’t think. At least not in a way I’ve noticed as a big problem.

I can get a little fidgety sometimes, like shifting around or messing with my hands, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly needing to move or anything. And I try really hard not to interrupt people—I’m pretty aware of that because I don’t want to come off rude.

Acting on impulse… I’m not sure. I don’t think I do that much. If anything, I probably overthink things. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have people close to you—like a partner, family member, or friend—ever pointed out that you seem to lose track mid-conversation or forget things you agreed to do outside of work?

Yeah… I guess more so at work than with family or friends, if that still counts.

Like when my supervisor tells me something face-to-face, I’ll be nodding and I really do think I’m listening. But then literally a minute later I’ll only remember the first part of what she said, and I have to ask someone else, “Wait, what did she say after that?” It’s kind of embarrassing, so I try to make it seem like I just need a quick clarification, not that I lost the whole middle of it.

Outside of work, I’m not sure people say it directly as much. But that’s the kind of thing that happens.

No new differential diagnoses emerged; anxiety, mood, or psychotic features were not endorsed.
